summary: This section explains the rules for choosing and running the offices of the Chairperson and Members of the Appellate Tribunal. It states that leaders appointed after a specific time in 2017 follow a different law called the Finance Act, 2017. Meanwhile, leaders appointed before that time continue to follow the older rules under this Act.
points: Applies to the Chairperson and other Members of the Appellate Tribunal.
Appoints leaders after the 2017 Finance Act using section 184 of that Act.
Covers qualifications, appointments, terms of office, pay, allowances, resignation, and removal.
Protects leaders appointed before the 2017 Finance Act to keep their original rules.
example: Suppose Apex Appellate Tribunal needs a new Chairperson after the start of the Finance Act of 2017. Under this section, the new Chairperson will have their qualifications, salary, and service terms decided by section 184 of the Finance Act, 2017, rather than the old Companies Act rules. Meanwhile, Mr. Roy, who was appointed as a Member before the Finance Act of 2017 came into force, does not need to worry. He will continue to be governed by the original rules of this Act and its old rules as if the 2017 law never changed anything for his position.

terms.meaning: A higher official body that hears and decides appeals against decisions made by a lower authority.
Despite or in spite of anything else mentioned.

watch: Do not mix up leaders appointed before and after the 2017 Finance Act, as they follow completely different rules.
